column2: We’ve officially hit the JS framework churn phase of AI tooling.
Why would you not use an open-source harness in October 2026? I am generally curious - what is the alpha?

I'm still waiting for one of these companies to provide the actual hard part.

The web front end (chat UI) that the business actually interacts with often needs to be adapted to the domain. We have tried to use the various chat UIs out of the box with customization on top and all of this has failed spectacularly. There are cases where we need to pop into an inline approval flow with custom elements and controller actions. How do you hook the existing platforms for this? There zero path. MCP can give you an information channel, but it does not enforce the required UI/UX flow for certain tool calls. We could either compromise on UX or rebuild chatgpt.com from scratch. We ultimately went with the latter.
What about an AgentFactoryFactory? That would increase Cursor's valuation from $60 to $120 billion.
Open AI and Anthropic already have "Agent SDK" brands. Vercel is "AI SDK". I wish folks would come up with some good names for new projects.

If you are on onstagram 99% of posts are people shilling skills where you need to subscribe to some service. To which they are an affiliate.

And a lot of the apps are the same thing.

It's going to be a race to the bottom.
Does anyone even use Cursor still? I loved it during the tab era but ever since they tried to catch up to agentic workflows, the product experience got worse and worse
I’ve been using Vercel’s Eve it’s really lovely for an agent that lives on a server somewhere (no affiliation)

The video is still showing @grok/agent-sdk.

Meanwhile, we know Grok Bot was really Cursor beforehand... it must be wild in there.

I'm starting to think that the LLMs ecosystem is going in the JS ecosystem direction, endless technologies with little to no adaption.

Literally everyday there is a new tool and the tools released last week are deprecated.

I have so many use cases for this. I just hope that we'll get a standard like https://www.openresponses.org/, because the idea of coupling an app to a particular vendor doesn't seem appealing at all, especially since it seems that the functionalities they offer are more or less the same. (I'm thinking about the OpenAI's Agent API and Anthropic's Agent SDK as "alternatives.)
Pi durable for me

Honest question, why shouldn't any agent SDK's API simply be a PROMPT.md with a runtime that runs the LLM with tools; why do you need excessive abstractions over that like langchain offers?

Is it to have boundaries of some determinism?
In 2026, the wheel that keeps getting reinvented is the agent harness.
